decision_reason: Compile-time const assertion binding StorageLimits::DEFAULT.max_journal_batch_bytes == DEFAULT_JOURNAL_BATCH_BYTES_INCLUSIVE_OF_HEADER (1_048_636) and == DEFAULT_JOURNAL_BATCH_BYTE_LIMIT + RECORD_HEADER_BYTES. Default budget of 1_048_636 must accommodate at least one max-size encoded event (RECORD_HEADER_BYTES 60 + MAX_JOURNAL_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES 1_048_576). Parity claim with existing kani_vb_vzcuf_ps007::check_bridge_accommodates_single_event preserved.

Code-review obligation to correct the misleading comment in crates/workspace_tests/tests/journal_batch_accounting_tests.rs:48-51 claiming JournalWriteBatch does not enforce byte limits. Behavior is not behavior-affecting (documentation only).

No new error variant for the queued path; reuse JournalError::JournalBatchBytesExceeded { attempted: u64, limit: u64 } with diagnostic code 0x4022 and symbolic code JOURNAL_BATCH_BYTES_EXCEEDED. Negative test asserts no QueuedBatchBytesExceeded variant exists.

MANDATORY parity test journal_write_batch_and_journal_writer_queue_emit_identical_error_for_same_oversize_event asserting variant == JournalBatchBytesExceeded AND attempted == direct.attempted AND limit == direct.limit AND code == 0x4022 AND symbol == JOURNAL_BATCH_BYTES_EXCEEDED.

Negative-space claim: enqueue_journaled and enqueue_strict MUST NOT enforce byte budget; only flush_batch does. Required unit test enqueue_does_not_enforce_byte_budget_only_flush_does enqueues many near-max events that would together exceed the budget, observes all enqueues succeed, observes flush_batch rejects.
drain_all must short-circuit on first JournalBatchBytesExceeded; no further flush_batch iterations. Required unit test drain_all_short_circuits_on_first_byte_budget_rejection.

Atomicity anchor: gate fires AFTER staged_keys_unique + durable_key_unique checks and BEFORE owned_batch.insert and owned_batch.commit(). On rejection, OwnedWriteBatch is dropped without commit; pending.len() unchanged. Required tests flush_batch_rejects_oversize_no_commit and flush_batch_at_capacity_partial_drain_then_oversize_rejected_no_commit.

Byte accumulator is stack-local u64 inside flush_batch; never a field on JournalWriterQueueState. Concurrency anchor: existing Mutex<JournalWriterQueueState> covers all state mutation; byte accumulator adds no shared mutable state.

Guard-precedence anchor: byte gate fires AFTER staged_keys_unique guard; existing test flush_batch_rejects_same_batch_duplicate_key continues to pass unmodified. New test flush_batch_duplicate_key_takes_precedence_over_byte_gate verifies DuplicateStagedKey is the surface error when both gates would reject.

checked_add overflow anchor: accumulator.checked_add(next) == None returns GateDecision::Reject { attempted: u64::MAX, limit }, mirroring JournalWriteBatch::append_event:86-102. Kani harness kani_vb_vzcuf_ps010::check_queued_byte_budget_invariants with kani::any() for accumulator/next/limit and explicit overflow sentinel assertion.
Exact-fit anchor: strict > comparison (not >=) accepts attempted == limit. Kani harness sub-check covers the equality boundary.

Type-system anchor: EncodedRecordLength and AccumulatedFlushBytes newtypes prevent payload-basis vs encoded-basis confusion. Kani harness bound to MAX_ENCODED_RECORD_BYTES (1_048_636) for symbolic event-size inputs.

Length-roundtrip property: for any JournalEvent accepted by encode_record, the encoded Vec<u8>.len() equals the byte count consumed by the gate (EncodedRecordLength::new(value.len() as u64)). Both direct and queued paths consume the same value.len() — encoded basis parity.

The queued-path gate is implemented as a pure newtype predicate over u64. Verus would require #[spec]/#[proof] annotations on the production source; the contract explicitly defers Verus work for the queued path. Existing Verus coverage of JournalWriteBatch (vb-vzcuf PS-006/PS-007) is preserved.
